results.name: family_leeds_budget
results.reply: Garforth East ranks top for a family on your budget, with strong health, community and environment scores and a median price of about £305k. Meanwood has the best education score of the leading areas, though its safety score is weaker, and Primley Park & Wigton Moor is close to your budget limit. I'd shortlist these three and then check street-level detail (LSOA) inside them, since safety and house prices vary a lot within a neighbourhood.

results.name: commuter_manchester
results.reply: I set the weighting to the commuter preset, which puts transport at the top. The highest-ranked neighbourhoods within 15 km are mostly inner-city areas right by the centre, such as New Islington South & Bradford and University North & Whitworth Street, with excellent transport scores but weak safety scores. For a calmer base with a shorter overall journey, Sale Central and Timperley North in Trafford score well on safety, schools and amenities, though they cost more to buy in. Pick any of these on the map to see the commute and cost trade-offs in more detail.

results.name: retiree_devon
results.reply: I ran the ranking on a retiree weighting that favours safety, quiet (noise and environment) and nearby health services. Searching "Devon" returned West Devon only, so I checked the main districts separately. The strongest quiet-and-safe neighbourhoods I found are Teignmouth North (Teignbridge), Exmouth Brixington (East Devon) and Budleigh Salterton (East Devon), which is the most expensive of the three. Mid Devon and Torridge are not yet checked. Each figure is measured against all scored neighbourhoods in the index.

results.name: safest_bristol
results.reply: The safest neighbourhoods near Bristol are Downend North and Emersons Green, but both sit in South Gloucestershire, just outside the city. The highest-ranked area inside Bristol itself is Westbury-on-Trym, in fourth place. This list covers a 10 km radius around Bristol, so I can narrow it to city-only areas if you'd like.

results.name: brighton_street_level_budget
results.reply: I ranked the 87 small areas within 10 km of Brighton that have typical prices under £400k, so some results sit outside the city proper. The top three are Seven Dials, Goldsmid East and Withdean Woods, and all ten are in Brighton and Hove. Several have low stability scores (Hove Central, Elm Grove and Goldsmid West), so their rankings may shift. Housing scores are weaker across the list, which fits the price cap.

results.name: young_professional_london
results.reply: Based on your nightlife and commute priorities, the top matches are Rotherhithe, East Village, Surrey Quays and Millwall South. They score very high on transport and amenities, with East Village and Rotherhithe typically around £475k–£530k. Their safety scores are lower, so it's worth checking the street-level detail. Clapham Common West is a strong all-rounder, but its median price is £905k, and Nightingale Lane's is £1.5m.

results.name: profile_postcode
results.reply: LS6 3AA is in Headingley, Leeds, and scores 65.5, better than 71% of England. It stands out for amenities, health services, and transport, with very short distances to a supermarket and GP. Safety is its weakest theme (burglary and theft are high), and sunshine and climate scores are low. Its house price figure rests on few sales, so treat it as approximate.

results.name: profile_place
results.reply: Whitley Bay Promenade, a small area of about 1,650 residents, scores 59.1 overall, better than 43% of England and Wales. It stands out for amenities, schools and health services, and for sunshine, but it scores poorly on safety (violent and anti-social behaviour rates), housing affordability, community and tree cover. Whitley Bay has other neighbourhoods, so I can profile or compare a few if you want a wider view.

results.name: compare_two
results.reply: Chapel Allerton North scores slightly higher overall (70.5 vs 68.1). Headingley leads on amenities and nightlife, transport and cheaper homes, while Chapel Allerton North is stronger on schools, safety (especially burglary) and environment. I compared the North Chapel Allerton neighbourhood, not the wider Chapel Allerton area, so check that is the one you mean.

results.name: compare_three_bristol
results.reply: Clifton Village scores highest overall (74), with strong schools, environment and community ratings, though housing affordability is weak. Redland & St Andrew's (71) is close behind, with the best health access and the highest prices (about £499k). Bedminster (61) trails mainly on safety, where violent-crime levels are much higher, but it is the most affordable of the three (about £323k) and has better housing scores.

results.name: well_run_pubs
results.reply: Eight well-run pubs (food hygiene rating 5) sit within about 500 m of SW1A 1AA, the closest being The Phoenix at roughly 260 m. Ratings only reflect hygiene, not beer or atmosphere, so check the pub itself before you go. Distances are straight-line.

results.name: nearest_gp
results.reply: The nearest GP to M1 1AE is New Islington Medical Centre (postcode M4 6EE), about 770 m away in straight-line distance. City Health Centre (M1 1PL) is a similar distance at about 780 m, so it's worth checking which one is taking new patients before you go.

results.name: explain_safety_gmp
results.reply: The safety score for Manchester 060A (Castlefield & Deansgate), the closest match I could find for the city centre, is 7.5 out of 100. The main drags are violence and sexual offences (84 per 1,000 residents a year), criminal damage and public order, and serious road collisions nearby. Because the rates use residents as the denominator, a central area with many visitors and few residents scores worse than its crime levels alone would suggest. Police data for Greater Manchester is also estimated, so treat the figures as indicative.

results.name: explain_high_score
results.reply: Hampstead Town (Camden 002C) scores 67, better than 77% of all areas in the index. It is strong on amenities, transport, schools, health services and climate, which together outweigh weak housing (house prices around £1.39m) and safety (theft, burglary and anti-social behaviour rates). The score covers one small area, not all of Hampstead, so neighbouring streets may differ.

results.name: least_noise_london
results.reply: The quietest London neighbourhoods by road, rail and industrial noise (share of homes exposed) are Greenwich Peninsula East, Belsize Park, Noel Park, Furzedown West and Homerton North, with under 8% of homes affected in each. The search covered areas within 10 km of central London, so outer boroughs were not included. Noise is only one factor, and some of these areas score lower on safety or housing affordability, so check the full profiles before shortlisting.

results.name: map_layer_air
results.reply: The map is now coloured by nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), the main air-quality measure in the index. Fine particles (PM2.5) are also scored, but I can colour by that instead if you'd prefer. Lower NO₂ means cleaner air.

results.name: shortlist_add
results.reply: Headingley in Leeds is now on your shortlist. I used the Leeds suburb, the top match for the name; Far Headingley and Headingley Hill are separate areas if you meant one of those.

results.name: what_is_measured_schools
results.reply: The schools and childcare theme scores four things: how good the primary schools nearby are (England only), how good the secondary schools nearby are (England, Wales and Scotland), how much choice of good schools there is (all four nations), and how good the nurseries nearby are (all four nations). Primary and secondary exam results are shown as context but don't count toward the score.

results.name: compare_top_two_followup
results.reply: Garforth East and Far Headingley & Weetwood are almost level overall (71.7 vs 71.5), but they trade off differently. Garforth East is safer (74 vs 45 on safety) and cheaper (£296k vs £316k typical price). Far Headingley is better connected, closer to a supermarket, and stronger on health services and amenities, though it has higher violent crime and burglary rates. Garforth suits buyers prioritising safety and value; Far Headingley suits those who want amenities and transport.

results.name: reweight_followup
results.reply: On the retiree weighting, Wigginton ranks first, with Haxby and South Bank & Dringhouses close behind. Wigginton and Haxby both score very highly on health (close GP and pharmacy access, per the retiree weights), and Strensall stands out for safety. The trade-off is amenities and transport, which are weaker in Wigginton, Haxby and Strensall than in the city-centre-adjacent areas. The page's sliders now reflect the retiree preset.

results.name: ambiguous_clapham
results.reply: I used Clapham in Lambeth, London (the neighbourhood is Clapham North). It scores 60.1, better than 48% of all areas in the index. It is strong on amenities, transport, schools and climate, but weak on housing affordability (typical price about £577,500) and safety, with robbery and theft well above the national norm. If you meant a village, there are also Claphams in North Yorkshire, Bedford, Arun and Teignbridge, and I can profile any of them.

results.name: ambiguous_newport
results.reply: There are several Newports, so I profiled the three most likely. **Newport city (Wales)**, in the Stow Hill neighbourhood, scores 65.3, better than 78% of Wales. It excels on health, amenities and transport but scores very low on safety and community. **Newport (Telford and Wrekin)**, in Newport South, scores 67.0, better than 78% of England, with strong schools and low crime relative to the city but weak rail access. **Newport (Isle of Wight)**, in Newport Central, scores 55.8, better than only 19% of England, held back by schools, rail and safety despite a sunny climate. Tell me which one you meant and I can dig deeper.

results.name: edinburgh_ranking
results.reply: Top balanced-weight picks in Edinburgh are Marchmont West, Canonmills and New Town North, Marchmont East and Sciennes, Bruntsfield, and Stockbridge, all scoring around 76–80 and strong on health, amenities and transport. The trade-off is housing: these central areas score low on affordability, with typical prices from about £335k to £597k. If you prioritise value, look at the Comely Bank or Inverleith results, or re-rank with a housing weighting.

results.name: glasgow_profile
results.reply: Hyndland resolved to the Dowanhill-01 small area (about 1,150 residents, Glasgow City), which scores better than 94% of neighbourhoods across the UK and Ireland. It is strong on schools, health services, amenities, environment and transport, with excellent tree cover and walkable services. The trade-offs are housing (typical price around £411k, in the bottom 4%), sunshine (in the bottom 13% for the UK) and road collision risk. If you want a sense of the wider Hyndland area, I can check its neighbouring small areas.

results.name: belfast_ranking
results.reply: The top-ranked Belfast neighbourhoods on the balanced weighting are mostly in the east and south-east: Ormiston (around Bangor-side Holywood Road area, east Belfast), Lisnasharragh and Castle N, all scoring high on transport, community and health. Ormiston and Lisnasharragh are the strongest all-round picks, though Lisnasharragh F and Castle N have lower stability scores, so treat their ranks with some caution. Education scores are blank for every area here, so the schools theme isn't reflected in these rankings; if schools matter to you, I can re-weight or profile specific areas.

Schools & childcare isn't scored for Northern Ireland, so it is left out of the overall score.

results.name: dublin_ranking
results.reply: The top-ranked neighbourhoods within 10 km of Dublin city centre are mostly in the southern suburbs: Stillorgan, Blackrock, Terenure and Clonskeagh. They score highly on health, transport, amenities and community, but safety is middling and the housing and education scores are missing here, so they don't reflect those. If price or schools matter to you, check the individual profiles before deciding.

results.name: ranelagh_profile

It is strong on health services, transport, amenities and community, but weak on safety (theft and burglary) and noise exposure. Schools and housing aren't scored for Ireland, so affordability needs checking separately.

results.name: ireland_retirees
